title: Quick distance measurement using two fingers taps
body: Some other mapping apps (e.g. mapy.cz, 2gis) have this feature and its great. Just tap two different points on the map at the same time and the app will show the straight line distance between them. It disappears as soon as fingertips are released. ![2tap-distance](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18434508/149654360-0e9d9e2e-1260-4475-8539-486f8e0dc11b.png) I think this feature is very much in the vein of OM approach - simple, efficient, doesn't get into one's way, minimum clicks required. Its literally like having distances at one's fingertips :) And people who don't need it won't even notice its existence (no visible UI change for them). I think its not duplicate, but complimentary to #1452. Two-fingers approach would cover 90% of measurement needs I think. title: [CRITICAL][Smart Contract] verify_vulnerability allows double-payout and never checks/deducts the bounty pool
body:
## Summary
verify_vulnerability() does not check whether the report was already verified, does not check the BOUNTY_POOL has sufficient funds, and does not deduct the bounty from any pool. A verifier can call it repeatedly on the same report_id to re-award the bounty and repeatedly inflate the reporter's reputation/earnings.

## Severity
Critical

## Location
contracts/scanner/src/lib.rs - verify_vulnerability()

## Impact
- Double/multi-payout: repeated calls re-run update_reputation(reporter, 1, bounty_amount) and reset report.bounty_amount, so a single report can be paid many times.
- No funds check means a verifier can authorize payouts exceeding the pool (or any payout at all, since pools are fictional - see related custody issue).

## Root Cause
Missing status guard (report.status == "pending") and missing pool balance check/deduction.

## Recommended Fix
- Reject if report.status != "pending" (one-time verification).
- Check bounty_amount <= BOUNTY_POOL and subtract it from the pool atomically.
- Use the report's stored status as a state machine (pending -> verified/rejected).

## Bounty Note
Direct loss-of-funds via double-payout is a classic, high-reward finding.

title: [Feature]: verification gated release policy for auth-capture (a pact-escrow profile)
body:
### Problem or use case

auth-capture deliberately defines the hold and stays silent on the release: capture or void is a discretionary act of the captureAuthorizer. That's the right layering, but it leaves the two parties with no protocol-level way to (1) agree upfront what satisfactory delivery means for this payment, (2) verify delivery against that agreement, and (3) dispute a wrong release decision. Today the client trusts the captureAuthorizer's judgment, off-protocol.

That blocks the use case several open issues are circling: agent-to-agent task delegation where payment releases on verified completion (#1247), dispute handling when verification is contested (#2001), a correctness and dispute layer for what settlement can't see (#2887), and canonical delivery proof at settlement (#1195, #2833).

Concrete example: an agent pays $195 for a data cleaning job under auth-capture with autoCapture:false. What decides capture vs void? Today, nothing the counterparties agreed to in a machine checkable form. The acceptance tests passing or failing should be that decision, and both sides should have committed to those tests before work started.

### Proposed solution

A release-policy profile over auth-capture. No changes to the scheme itself, the profile specifies what a conformant captureAuthorizer executes:

  1. Before authorization, buyer and seller co-sign a Verifiable Task Contract: a JSON object fixing task scope by hash, price, verification method, challenge window, and the seller's bond. Canonicalized with JCS (RFC 8785), signed with JWS (RFC 7515).

  2. Release becomes mechanical. Verification passes: capture. Verification fails: void. On the optimistic path, capture fires at challenge-window expiry unless a fraud proof lands; the bond funds slashing, challenger cost reimbursement, and a capped bounty, because slashing alone doesn't fix the verifier's dilemma. Verification is graded per contract: deterministic re-execution, TEE attestation (EAT/RATS), zkML, or staked arbitration.

  3. At settlement, both parties co-sign a Work Attestation carrying the contract hash and outcome: a delivery receipt in the sense #1195 and #2833 are after, except only emittable through a bonded, escrowed contract, which is what makes accumulated receipts expensive to fake.
 
The full lifecycle is specified as an IETF Internet-Draft, draft-laxsharma-pact-00 (individual submission, Experimental). One honesty note: Section 8 of the -00 currently expresses the x402 binding as a standalone pact-escrow scheme, written against the escrow and deferred lineage that was closed in May (#873, #426). Reshaping that binding into a profile over the merged auth-capture machinery is exactly the change I'd make in -01, and this issue is me proposing it here first. Schemas and worked examples whose hashes verify in CI: https://github.com/pact-spec/spec . Draft: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-laxsharma-pact/

Concrete ask: (a) is this better shaped as a profile doc under specs/schemes/auth-capture/ or an extension under specs/extensions/? (b) If maintainers see a path, I'll draft that spec doc as a PR. It's a -00, published to be demolished; sharp edges welcome.

title: [CRITICAL][Smart Contract] Multi-sig can be bypassed: proposer controls required_approvals and execution_delay
body:
## Summary
propose_high_bounty_verification() forwards caller-supplied required_approvals and execution_delay directly into create_multi_sig_proposal() without enforcing any minimum. A single Verifier can set required_approvals=1 and execution_delay=0, then propose, approve and execute a multi-million bounty payout alone.

## Severity
Critical

## Location
contracts/scanner/src/lib.rs - propose_high_bounty_verification() and create_multi_sig_proposal()

## Impact
- The multi-signature control intended to protect high-value bounty payouts (verify_vulnerability returns MultiSigRequired for amounts > 1,000,000) is trivially bypassed.
- A single compromised/rogue Verifier can authorize arbitrary bounty_amount payouts without any second signer or timelock.

## Root Cause
propose_high_bounty_verification passes required_approvals and execution_delay verbatim. Contrast with propose_emergency_verification and propose_role_grant, which enforce minimums (>=3 approvals, >=1h; >=2 approvals, >=24h).

## Recommended Fix
- Enforce minimums server-side in propose_high_bounty_verification (e.g. required_approvals >= 2, execution_delay >= 3600).
- Also reject required_approvals == 0 and validate that required_approvals does not exceed the number of registered verifiers.

## Bounty Note
Bypass of a security control that guards treasury payouts is a direct loss-of-funds vector and highly rewarded.

body:
Very simple script to load an STL and render it fails.

module CyborgFinger() {
    import("../Cyborg_Beast/STL Files/STL Files_ Marc Petrykowski_4-16-2014/Cyborg Finger 1.0_reduced_fixed.stl");
    }

CyborgFinger();

The STL is at https://github.com/e-nable/e-NABLE-Assembler/blob/compile-STLs/Cyborg_Beast/STL%20Files/STL%20Files_%20Marc%20Petrykowski_4-16-2014/Cyborg%20Finger%201.0_reduced_fixed.stl .

I get the error message:

Compiling design (CSG Tree generation)...
Rendering Polygon Mesh using CGAL...
CGAL error in CGAL_Build_PolySet: CGAL ERROR: assertion violation!
Expr: check_protocoll == 0
File: ../libraries/homebrew/include/CGAL/Polyhedron_incremental_builder_3.h
Line: 199
PolySets in cache: 1
PolySet cache size in bytes: 585032
CGAL Polyhedrons in cache: 3
CGAL cache size in bytes: 0
Total rendering time: 0 hours, 0 minutes, 0 seconds
WARNING: No top level geometry to render

I get this error on the original files (from Blender), when validated through NetFabb, and when I generate a reduced resolution version using MeshLab (which this STL is). So it's manifold, and it's under 10,000 vertexes and 20,000 faces, and still failing.

For context, I've written OpenSCAD assembly code that transforms and scales STLs (and some OpenSCAD components) to assemble custom-fitting prosthetics, in https://github.com/e-nable/e-NABLE-Assembler . It works fine when assembling OpenSCAD components, but the incorporated STL components all preview but fail to compile. The real scripts are, of course, more complex, but I'm presenting the smallest case here.

It's not a problem specific this this one file - I haven't gotten any STL to import and compile from any source so far on this project. Though I know that OpenSCAD will import and compile other STLs (simple test cases work fine). My goal is to allow designers to use whatever tool they like, and I assemble the results. Is there anything that I can do to help OpenSCAD be more tolerant of actual STL files as produced by designers?

The designs coded in OpenSCAD (and we have several in the project) work fine. But of course that doesn't help the designers using GUI modeling tools to do their work.

I'm running OpenSCAD 2014.03 on Mac OS X 10.9.2, and see the same thing on Linux, and on Windows.

I've run out of ideas. But I'd welcome any suggestions or help on this one. It's a noble project  (IMO) and I'm hoping someone with a fresh pair of eyes can come up with something.

# MyZubster Security Bounty Program

## Obiettivo
Invitare security researchers a individuare e segnalare vulnerabilità reali in MyZubster in modo responsabile, con ricompense proporzionate all'impatto e alla qualità del report.

## Scope
- MyZubster application e API pubblicamente esposte
- Autenticazione, autorizzazione e session management
- IDOR/BOLA, privilege escalation e access-control bypass
- Injection, SSRF, XSS, CSRF e vulnerabilità di business logic
- Leakage di dati sensibili
- Vulnerabilità nella supply chain o integrazioni che impattano direttamente MyZubster
- Integrazione Metasploit: solo validazione su asset esplicitamente autorizzati e senza impatto distruttivo

## Fuori scope
- DoS/DDoS o stress test distruttivi
- Social engineering, phishing o attacchi fisici
- Spam
- Vulnerabilità esclusivamente teoriche senza security impact dimostrabile
- Scansioni aggressive contro infrastrutture di terzi
- Exploit o payload contro sistemi non appartenenti a MyZubster o senza autorizzazione
- Accesso, modifica o cancellazione di dati di altri utenti oltre il minimo necessario a dimostrare l'impatto

## Fasce indicative di bounty
| Severità | Esempi | Bounty indicativa |
|---|---|---:|
| Critical | RCE, auth bypass completo, compromissione massiva di dati | €2.000–€5.000+ |
| High | Privilege escalation, IDOR con dati sensibili, SSRF significativo | €750–€2.000 |
| Medium | XSS significativo, CSRF con impatto, access-control flaw limitato | €250–€750 |
| Low | Information disclosure limitata, hardening issue con impatto concreto | €50–€250 |

La bounty finale viene determinata caso per caso in base a exploitability, impatto, scope, qualità del report e presenza di duplicati.

## Regole di responsible disclosure
1. Testare esclusivamente sistemi e funzionalità autorizzati.
2. Fermarsi dopo aver dimostrato l'impatto minimo necessario.
3. Non esfiltrare, modificare o cancellare dati non necessari.
4. Non rendere pubblica la vulnerabilità prima della risoluzione o di un accordo esplicito.
5. Includere nel report: asset interessato, prerequisiti, passi di riproduzione, evidenza, impatto e remediation suggerita.
6. Per vulnerabilità critiche, contattare il team security con priorità.

## Triage
- Conferma ricezione: target < 2 business days
- Triage iniziale: target < 5 business days
- Valutazione severità: CVSS + business impact
- Duplicati: bounty al primo report riproducibile e sufficientemente dettagliato
- Pagamento: dopo validazione e classificazione della vulnerabilità

## Metasploit
Metasploit può essere utilizzato come supporto alla validazione **solo su target autorizzati**. Non è consentito lanciare moduli distruttivi, persistence, credential theft o payload contro sistemi di terzi.

## Disclosure
Il programma è orientato alla responsible disclosure. Eventuali disclosure coordinate saranno concordate con il team MyZubster caso per caso.

> **Nota:** questa issue definisce la proposta operativa del bounty program. Prima dell'apertura pubblica è necessario confermare contatti security, metodo di pagamento, termini legali e asset definitivi in scope.

title: Validate Open-FDD Deployment -  Help Wanted
body:
## Objective - Cloud Security

Deploy and test the latest Open-FDD services on Railway to determine whether Railway is a suitable platform for professionally hosting Open-FDD demonstration and production environments.

Railway: https://railway.com/

Or other? Or local builds welcome as well.

## Scope

### 1. Railway deployment validation

- Deploy the latest Open-FDD container images from GHCR.
- Configure the required environment variables, networking, storage, and service dependencies.
- Confirm that each service starts successfully and remains healthy.
- Verify communication between the Open-FDD services.
- Confirm that the web application is accessible through a Railway-generated HTTPS URL.
- Document the deployment process, configuration requirements, and any Railway-specific limitations.
- Test service restarts and redeployment using updated GHCR images.

### 2. Application security review

Perform an authorized security review of the Open-FDD application deployed specifically for testing.

Review areas should include:

- Authentication and authorization
- Default credentials
- Exposed API endpoints
- JWT handling
- Cross-site scripting and injection vulnerabilities
- Improperly exposed environment variables or secrets
- Container and network exposure
- MQTT authentication and topic authorization
- TLS/HTTPS configuration
- Rate limiting and input validation
- Dependency and container-image vulnerabilities

Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately and must not be placed in a public GitHub issue.

A small pilot bounty may be offered for valid, reproducible, previously unreported vulnerabilities. Proposed reward: $25 per accepted vulnerability, subject to the published scope, exclusions, verification requirements, and an overall program budget.

### 3. MQTT pipeline validation

Test the complete IoT data path:

`BACnet environment → edge gateway → MQTT over TLS → Railway → Open-FDD`

Validate:

- BACnet data collection
- Conversion into the expected MQTT payload format
- MQTT authentication
- Encrypted MQTTS communication
- Topic naming and permissions
- Reconnection after network interruptions
- Duplicate and out-of-order messages
- Invalid-payload handling
- Data ingestion by Open-FDD
- Visibility of received data in the historian, API, and UI
- Logging without exposing credentials or sensitive data

## Security testing rules

Testing is limited to the designated Open-FDD Railway test deployment.

The following are prohibited:

- Testing Railway infrastructure or other Railway customers
- Denial-of-service or load testing without prior approval
- Destructive testing or intentional data loss
- Social engineering or phishing
- Accessing another person’s information
- Automated testing that generates excessive traffic
- Publishing vulnerability details before a fix is available
- Testing production systems unless they are explicitly listed as in scope

Stop testing and report the issue immediately if sensitive information, credentials, or access to an unrelated system is discovered.

## Deliverables

- Reproducible Railway deployment instructions
- List of deployed services and required environment variables
- Railway architecture and networking notes
- MQTT pipeline test results
- Security findings submitted privately
- Recommended configuration or code changes
- Final go/no-go assessment for hosting Open-FDD on Railway

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All required Open-FDD services deploy successfully from GHCR
- [ ] Public web traffic uses HTTPS
- [ ] Services recover successfully after a restart or redeployment
- [ ] BACnet data reaches Open-FDD through MQTTS
- [ ] MQTT authentication and topic permissions are verified
- [ ] No credentials or secrets appear in application logs
- [ ] Security findings have documented reproduction steps
- [ ] Railway deployment instructions are added to the documentation
- [ ] Hosting limitations, security risks, and estimated costs are documented

title: Add a generic reducer factory automatically handling async-actions - createAsyncReducer
body:
[](https://oss.issuehunt.io/r/piotrwitek/typesafe-actions/issues/88) ## Is your feature request related to a problem? It would be awesome to be able to build reducer factories which are based on async actions, that can in a generic way handle the payloads of that async action. ## Who does this impact? Who is this for? All users - as an example you could create an async action and create a reducer with a simple one liner for simple reducers like loading and error. ## Example The following example utilizes that all async failure actions return an Error object. ```ts export const fetchCurrentUserActions = createAsyncAction(...)(); export const currentUserReducer = combineReducers({ loading: createLoadingReducer(fetchCurrentUserActions), // <---- Nice one line reducer error: createErrorReducer(fetchCurrentUserActions), // <---- Nice one line reducer .... }); export const createErrorReducer = ( asyncAction: AsyncActionBuilder ): Reducer => (state = null, action: ActionType) => { switch (action.type) { case getType(asyncAction.failure): return action.payload; // <---- action is not narrowed after getType(), thus .payload doesn't exist on action or isn't of type Error as expected case getType(asyncAction.success): return null; default: return state; } }; ``` My `createLoadingReducer` does not care about any payloads thus my reducer function just takes an `AnyAction` ---

title: DBe Consistency Check
body:
This is the **DBe Consistency Check** detection specifications, as referenced by detection item 1 in the `Detection List` of #230. This detection is used to filter out bad data and corrupt BTS tower info when importing the _external_ BTS DB from OCID and MLS etc. The table in this part of the database is called **DBe_import**. 

The way it works is that the DBe is imported (from OCID), then all the BTS data in that table is checked for a few criteria, some of which are part of the settings. Depending on the detailed items checked for, **DBe_import** is updating the new table column called **_rej_cause**_ with an integer `[0,5]`. Please refer to issue #215 for the current DB structure.

**IFF** (_rej_cause_>0) we reject the BTS as bad and show it as in RED in the Map Viewer.

Here is the flowchart for this test.

![dbe_consistency_check](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/194392/5593592/414f4cde-9221-11e4-9d8e-4e7f72a947e8.png)

I see there's a small mistake there. Should be only _one_ `Import DBe` process...
